Messages.Body:
My Nosferatu Shadow-warriors lost their first ever game last night,
though not by much. During that game the following situation arose:

Tura Vaughn bled, i woke Chester with rat's warning, prevented, pressed,
tapped the Spawning pool at the start of the next round and played taste
of vitae to gain all the blood Tura lost BEFORE she could play Majesty to
scuttle off back to brujah-land.

Is this ok?

i increasingly think that Spawning Pool is a dam' fine card, given enough
rat's warnings and mighty grapples, and the taste aspect [whether or not
the above example is actually legal] makes me even more confident about
that statement.

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
t_e...@my-deja.com wrote:
> Not only that, I always thought that the Spawning Pool Damage was
> treated as Environmental Damage, so that you couldn't even use the ToV
> to get back the blood. If not so, I'm gonna take the 4 Spawning pools
> out of my trade list as this would greatly increase it's usebility.
>
> LSJ??? What is the ruling on this issue?

Taste of Vitae counts blood that the opposing vampire spent to heal
damage (or prevent destruction). It doesn't care whether the damage
was environmental or not.

After strike resolution (as required by ToV), you can play taste
to gain the blood that the opposing vampire spent healing damage,
even the blood he spent healing damage done by Spawning Pool (or
Weather Control, etc.)
